title: Lack of other molecules in CO-rich debris discs: is it primordial or secondary gas?
question: Whether the gas in CO-rich debris discs is a remnant from the earlier Class II phase (hybrid scenario) or of secondary origin driven by icy planetesimal destruction, tested via millimeter observations of simple molecules.

what.value: Rest frequencies of molecular transitions from the Splatalogue database

evidence.quote: Rest frequencies are taken from the Splatalogue database (<https://www.cv.nrao.edu/php/splat/>).

what.value: Unattenuated photodissociation rates and shielding functions

evidence.quote: The unattenuated photodissociation rates, as well as the corresponding shielding functions, were taken from (cite: heays2017).

what.value: Basic properties of the CO gas component (R_in, R_out, M_CO) in the debris disc subsample

evidence.quote: Basic properties of CO gas component in the debris disc subsample. The listed CO mass estimates are based on analysis of optically thin C$^{18}$O line observations. References in the last column: (1): (cite: kospal2013); (2): (cite: kral2019); (3): (cite: moor2017); (4): Pawellek et al. (in prep.).

external_data.citation: (cite: kospal2013); (cite: kral2019); (cite: moor2017); Pawellek et al. (in prep.)

what.value: Gas-grain chemical network from the KIDA'17 database with recent updates

evidence.quote: These physical conditions have been used to calculate time-dependent chemical evolution using the single-point ALCHEMIC chemical kinetics code and an up-to-date gas-grain chemical network (based on the KIDA’17 database with recent updates; (cite: KIDA; kida15)).
The first so-called “low metals” set of mainly atomic abundances from (cite: Lee_ea98) describes the elemental content of the ISM that is available for gas or icy chemistry.

what.value: Collisional cross-section and spectroscopic data from LAMDA

evidence.quote: The collisional cross-section and other spectroscopic data from the Leiden Atomic and Molecular Database (LAMDA) have been utilised (cite: lamda).

Since $^{13}$C and $^{18}$O are not included in the chemical network, we have used fixed isotopic ratios C$^{12}$/C$^{13} = 77$ and O$^{16}$/O$^{18} = 560$ to scale down the resulting molecular abundances (cite: wilson_rood_1994_isotope_ratio).

what.value: CN hyperfine components for brightness temperature calculation

evidence.quote: We have calculated the CN brightness temperature using hyperfine components from (cite: 2015MNRAS.446.1750F).

recipe.goal: Calibrate visibilities, subtract continuum, and image molecular line cubes
recipe.method: Calibrate and flag raw datasets with standard ALMA scripts in CASA, subtract continuum in uv-space with first-order polynomials using UVCONTSUB, and image spectral cubes with TCLEAN using natural weighting.
key_parameters: Natural weighting; channel widths rebinned to 0.9 km s^-1 (C2H, HCO+, HCN), 0.75 km s^-1 (CN), and 1.25 km s^-1 (coarse Band 6)

recipe.goal: Measure integrated line fluxes and 3-sigma upper limits from moment-0 maps
recipe.method: Construct zeroth-moment maps over line velocity ranges, measure fluxes using fitted elliptical apertures, estimate uncertainties from 16 random background apertures, and derive 3-sigma upper limits for non-detections using HCN or IMSMOOTH-smoothed archival 12CO cubes as templates.
key_parameters: 16 random background apertures for uncertainty; 3-sigma upper limits
assumptions: Expected velocity ranges and spatial extents of non-detected lines match those of HCN (for protoplanetary discs) or 12CO (for debris discs and HD 141569)

recipe.goal: Calculate molecular photodissociation lifetimes under H2 and C shielding
recipe.method: Compute photodissociation rates k = k0 * theta and lifetimes tau = 1/k as a function of H2 or neutral atomic carbon column density using literature unattenuated rates and shielding functions.
assumptions: Only the interstellar UV radiation field is taken into account; dust attenuation is negligible in debris discs

recipe.goal: Simulate time-dependent chemical evolution and non-LTE line radiative transfer
recipe.method: Run the single-point ALCHEMIC chemical kinetics code over a 2D temperature-density grid for 1 Myr across five sets of initial abundances (varying H2/He depletion), then compute non-LTE line brightness temperatures and flux ratios with RADEX.
key_parameters: Temperature grid: 10 to 300 K; density grid: 10^3 to 10^7 cm^-3; evolution time: 1 Myr; radial UV optical depth tau = 0 to 1; cosmic ray ionisation rate: 1.3e-17 s^-1; H2 depletion factors: 1, 2, 5, 10, 100
Emitting gas column length = 15 au; line FWHM = 1 km s^-1
assumptions: Dust-to-gas mass ratio set to 10^-10 for 0.1 um grains; unattenuated UV field equal to vertical ISRF; stellar X-rays and high-energy particles neglected; fixed isotopic ratios 12C/13C = 77 and 16O/18O = 560

recipe.goal: Calculate the effect of hydrogen depletion on gas molar mass and disc vertical scale height
recipe.method: Scale elemental abundances of species heavier than H2 and He by factors of 1 to 10^6, reshuffle into CO, H2O, and H2, and compute gas molar mass and hydrostatic vertical scale height for an isothermal 30 K disc.
key_parameters: Heavy element scaling factor: 1 to 10^6; disc temperature: 30 K
assumptions: Hydrostatic equilibrium; isothermal 30 K geometrically thin disc; all carbon locked in CO, remaining O and H in water (with and without water formation cases), remaining H in H2

score_reason: ALMA project codes, calibrators, spectral setups, and basic CASA tasks (UVCONTSUB, TCLEAN with natural weighting, channel rebinning) are clearly documented, and the chemical/radiative transfer modelling parameters (ALCHEMIC + RADEX) are well specified. However, exact aperture geometries, velocity integration windows, CASA version, and archival CO dataset identifiers are not explicitly stated.
rediscovery_reason: The raw ALMA data from projects 2017.1.01545.S and 2018.1.01429.S are public in the ALMA archive, the data reduction and aperture-flux extraction recipe is straightforward, and the main observational results are concrete numeric integrated line fluxes and 3-sigma upper limits (Table 3).
